subject: Hospitality
title: César Ritz: Inventing Luxury
description: One-minute skill: César Ritz: Inventing Luxury.

hook.text: César Ritz was the 13th child of a Swiss shepherd. He became 'the king of hoteliers and the hotelier of kings.'

buildup.text: Working his way up from waiter, Ritz learned that details matter: the perfect lighting, fresh flowers, impeccable attire.

discovery.text: At the Savoy in London, Ritz transformed standards. Every room had its own bathroom—a radical luxury in the 1890s.

twist.text: Ritz was fired from the Savoy over a financial dispute. He responded by opening the Ritz Paris—his masterpiece—in 1898.

climax.text: His name became an English word: 'ritzy.' No other hotelier has ever become a synonym for luxury itself.

punchline.text: Shepherd's son to a dictionary word. Ritz defined luxury hospitality.

quiz.question: Why was César Ritz fired from the Savoy?
options: A financial dispute with the owners
He was too demanding of staff
